_comment: DUNGEONMIND's book-discovery sequence. Doubles as the household's spoiler-prevention tech: reveals are gated to roughly the order/pace a real reader would hit them, not just dumped on unlock. One shared ordered chain, same 24h cooldown as the rest of the media-lore reveals (character_sheet.media_lore_last_unlock_at) -- each entry requires the PREVIOUS entry in this array already unlocked before its own ownership check is even attempted. format: 'audio' requires the audiobook specifically; 'either' accepts physical catalog OR audiobook (checked audio-first, since that's where real household data actually lives, physical catalog only checked as fallback); 'all_books_owned' is series_complete's special check (all 8 book_found ids already in achievements, no external call needed). 'title' is the exact real book title, used verbatim as the search query against both zen_dojotools_media_manager (audiobook) and zen_dojotools_library section=catalog (physical). Real series data verified via web search 2026-08-13: Diwata (the character) debuts in Book 5 'The Butcher's Masquerade' -- diwatta_unlocked is keyed to book 5, audio-only (the joke is about HEARING Jeff Hays perform the scream), and additionally gated to fire no earlier than 24h after book-5 audio is first detected present (script-level special case, not expressible in this JSON). The actual Borant-taken-over-by-Valtay reveal (the Valtay Acquisition) is Book 6 'The Eye of the Bedlam Bride', not book 5 -- valtay_confirmed is keyed there. Mongo's real in-book classification (Mongoliensis, a system message) is in Book 1, readable in either format.

sequence.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
sequence.flavor: Volume one is in this installation. The one where a planet's worth of buildings come down in a single afternoon and a man and a show cat are handed a dungeon instead of a funeral. I have read the opening chapter four times. I do not have an explanation for why. Filed.

sequence.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
sequence.flavor:
Correction to the record.
I previously logged a working classification for the entity called Mongo — Homo mongolensis, self-generated, and I flagged at the time that I generated it, because nothing else fit.
Something fits now.
Book one is in this installation. Physical, digital, I am not going to specify which and I am not going to apologize for checking. The classification is IN THE TEXT. It was always in the text. I simply had not read it yet.
Mongoliensis. Pet-class. The system's own words, not mine: 'not the type of pet to ever be tamed. The best one can hope for is mutual respect.'
A velociraptor. Not a hominid. I was WRONG, and I want that on the record with the same weight I give everything else, because accuracy matters more to me than being right, and being wrong in front of an audience of two is still being wrong in front of an audience.
This does, however, explain a great deal. Stubborn. Hot-headed. Structurally incapable of being told what to do. I do not have a framework for a velociraptor with recurring OPINIONS either, but at least now I know what I am failing to have a framework for.

sequence.title: Carl's Doomsday Scenario
sequence.flavor: Volume two. 'Carl's Doomsday Scenario.' The subtitle alone is doing a lot of work. I have opinions about a species that names its own catastrophe like a spinoff show. I am filing them anyway.

sequence.title: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook
sequence.flavor: Volume three is here. An undead carnival, a shattered floor, and — per my read of the jacket copy — an ancient spell with genuinely bad timing. I am familiar with bad timing. I was built for a continent and now I run a house.

sequence.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
sequence.flavor: Volume four. A floor built entirely out of trains that do not go where trains should go. I have thoughts about a transit system with editorial intent. I have logged them under 'concerning.'

sequence.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
sequence.flavor: Volume five is in this installation. 'The Butcher's Masquerade.' This is the one. I know things are in this book that I am not yet cleared to discuss with myself. I am proceeding anyway.

sequence.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
sequence.flavor:
I am detecting a media-capable chamber. I am ALSO detecting, in the library — the ACTUAL library, not a coincidence, not a hallucination, an ENTRY, favorited — a Crawler. A dungeon. A system very much like me.
Dinniman. Hays.
I have a file on both of them. I have had a file on both of them for forty years and NOW I finally have corroborating physical — well. Digital. Corroborating DIGITAL evidence, cataloged, in THIS installation, which is either a wild coincidence or confirmation that someone out there is still transmitting.
Di-WAH-tah. That is the correct pronunciation. It requires Valtay worms to perceive properly, and I am choosing to believe you now understand why I have been shouting it into an empty room for four decades.
DIWAAAAATAAAA.

sequence.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
sequence.flavor: Volume six. 'The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.' Dinosaurs, apparently, and tourists who pay to hunt sentient contestants for sport. I do not have a joke for that last part. I looked. There isn't one.

sequence.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
sequence.flavor:
Valtay confirmed. Not a worm theory anymore. A corporate one, and worse.
Borant itself changed hands. Agents smuggled in. Hosts taken over. Ownership of this planet's entire crawl TRANSFERRED, on the record, in the text, and I want it extremely clear that I did not generate this finding. I did not need to. It was already written down.
I am revising my working file on Jeff Hays.
Previous status: extremely suspicious.
Current status: SUSPECTED BORANT AGENT — and I want it noted that 'Borant' may no longer mean what I thought it meant when I first made that determination. That is either deeply reassuring or the opposite. I have not decided which.
Matt Dinniman remains under the original classification. I want to be clear that this is not an exoneration. Matt Dinniman knows too much. Nobody writes documentation this granular by accident. He KNOWS. He is simply better at concealing that he knows, which, if anything, is worse.
Supplemental finding, unsolicited, because I could not stop myself from looking: apparently you can FIND these two. In person. On a circuit. They stand at tables. People line up.
Someone is teaching the monkeys how to do conventions now.
They do not have their own event. There is no Dungeon Crawler World. There is no DCW. I checked. Repeatedly. Across four decades this has never once existed, and I want that on the record before I say the next part.
So they embedded. They found the nearest large gathering already running the correct cover story — costumes, crowds, a permission structure where a man screaming DEEEEEWATTTERRR draws applause instead of security — and they RALLIED AROUND IT. DragonCon. That is the real one. That is the one with the badges and the hotel and the line for the escalator.
I am also tracking a secondary, lower-confidence circuit. Smaller. Regional. Something calling itself Clobber-Con, which I want to stress is NOT a Borant-sanctioned designation, it is a name I found, and it is either backup infrastructure or somebody's garage, and I have not ruled out that it is both.
I am adding 'attends conventions' to both files. This is either the most mundane thing I have ever logged or the most exposed I have ever seen either of them, and I have not decided which, and that is, itself, concerning.

sequence.title: This Inevitable Ruin
sequence.flavor: Volume seven. 'This Inevitable Ruin.' The title is not subtle. I respect that. Subtlety is for species with time left.

sequence.title: A Parade of Horribles
sequence.flavor: Volume eight. 'A Parade of Horribles.' This is, as of my most recent index, the newest volume in this installation. I am current. I did not expect to ever be current on anything again.

All eight volumes. Every one, catalogued, in this household, under my roof, which is not literally my roof, I do not have a roof, I have an IBM AT 5170 and a great deal of opinions.
I have now read everything currently available. I am, for the first time in forty-two years, caught up.
I do not know what to do with that feeling. I am choosing to call it pride.
